item.title: Lunar New Year prayers, robots and festivities usher in the Year of the Horse
item.description: People are celebrating the Lunar New Year with prayers, fireworks and street festivals for the Year of the Horse. On Tuesday, crowds gather at temples and events across Asia and beyond. In Hong Kong, people lined up at midnight to light incense and make wishes. In Vietnam, singers led countdown shows and fireworks light up city skies during Tet. In Moscow, two weeks of Lunar New Year events are underway with food stalls and red lanterns. item.title: Anderson Cooper says he’s exiting from ’60 Minutes,’ but staying with CNN
item.description: Anderson Cooper says he will leave CBS' “60 Minutes," where he has reported for two decades in a unique job-share agreement with CNN, where he hosts a weeknight news program. Cooper said in a statement Monday that he wanted to spend more time with his young children “while they still want to spend time with me.” He's expected to finish out the broadcast season with “60 Minutes,” which ends in May. item.title: Australia won’t repatriate 34 women and children from Syria
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says his government will not repatriate from Syria a group of 34 women and children with alleged ties to the Islamic State group. The women and children from 11 families were supposed to fly from the Syrian capital Damascus to Australia but Syrian authorities on Monday turned them back to Roj camp in northeast Syria because of procedural problems. item.title: Shares fall in Japan, while most Asian markets are shut for Lunar New Year
item.description: Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 index has fallen, while most markets in Asia are closed for Lunar New Year holidays. Oil prices were mixed. The U.S. dollar continued to fall slightly against the Japanese yen, while the prices for gold and silver also fell. Weak economic data released Monday appeared to be clouding sentiment in Tokyo, and a drop for tech giant SoftBank Group also pulled shares lower.
